instrument_name: IRS Publication 15 (2026) Employer's Tax Guide - What's New: supplemental wage rates, backup withholding, information-return threshold, household/election worker thresholds
article_or_section: What's New; sec. 7 Supplemental Wages; Backup withholding
figure_or_rule_carried: Supplemental wages: optional flat 22%; mandatory 37% on supplemental wages above 1,000,000 paid to one employee in the calendar year (P.L. 119-21 permanent). Backup withholding 24%. Information-return and W-2-without-withholding threshold raised 600 -> 2,000 for payments after 2025 (indexed after 2026). FICA on household workers paid 3,000+ cash in 2026; election workers 2,500+ in 2026. Tips subject to FIT/FICA if 20+ in a month. Qualified moving-expense reimbursement exclusion permanently eliminated (except Armed Forces / intelligence community). Employment tax records kept at least 4 years.

instrument_name: IRS Publication 15 (2026) sec. 11 Depositing Taxes - lookback, monthly/semiweekly schedule, 100,000 next-day rule, 2026 DC legal holidays
article_or_section: Sec. 11 When To Deposit; Table 2 Semiweekly Deposit Schedule; Legal holiday
figure_or_rule_carried: Lookback for 2026 (Form 941 filers) = 2024-07-01..2025-06-30; Form 943/944/945 filers = CY2024. Taxes reported <= 50,000 -> monthly depositor (deposit by the 15th of the following month); > 50,000 -> semiweekly (Wed/Thu/Fri paydays -> following Wednesday; Sat/Sun/Mon/Tue -> following Friday). 100,000 or more accumulated on any day -> deposit next business day (either schedule). New 941 employer = monthly for its first calendar year. Separate deposits for 943 vs 941/944 taxes. Deposit legal holidays = DC legal holidays (2026 list incl. 2026-04-16 DC Emancipation Day). Electronic deposit (EFTPS).

Quarterly Form 941 amounts in cents.

instrument_name: 29 U.S.C. 207(a)(1) FLSA overtime (U.S. Code 2024 ed.)
figure_or_rule_carried: Non-exempt employees: overtime at not less than 1.5 x regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek (no federal daily overtime; daily OT is state law, e.g. CA/AK/NV/CO). The 0.5 premium portion = 'qualified overtime compensation' for the P.L. 119-21 deduction and W-2 Box 12 code TT (US-FEDS5-007).

instrument_name: 26 CFR 301.6109-4 IRS truncated taxpayer identification numbers (TTIN), eCFR current
figure_or_rule_carried: TTIN = SSN/ITIN/ATIN/EIN with the first five digits replaced by X or *, format XXX-XX-1234. Example in the regulation: employer may truncate the employee SSN on copies of Form W-2 furnished to the employee (31.6051-1(a)(1)(i)); never on Copy A filed with SSA; EIN not truncated (W-2 instructions). No federal statute requires SSN truncation on pay statements - state law per state unit.

instrument_name: 15 U.S.C. 1673 CCPA restriction on garnishment (U.S. Code 2024 ed.) - local copy
figure_or_rule_carried: Ordinary garnishment: max = lesser of 25% of weekly disposable earnings or disposable earnings above 30 x federal minimum hourly wage (30 x 7.25 = 217.50/week). Support orders: 50% if supporting a spouse/dependent child, 60% if not; +5 points (55%/65%) where arrears older than 12 weeks. Exceptions: bankruptcy court orders, federal/state tax debts (IRS levy -> Pub. 1494, US-FEDS5-014). Local file for US-FED-011, which had none.

instrument_name: 42 U.S.C. 653a(b)-(c) employer new-hire reporting (U.S. Code 2024 ed.) - local copy
figure_or_rule_carried: Report to the State Directory of New Hires of the state where the employee works: employee name, address, SSN, date services first performed (federal minimum fields; states may add, e.g. DOB, state of hire); employer name, address, FEIN. Deadline: not later than 20 days after hire, or for electronic filers 2 monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart. Multistate employers transmitting electronically may designate ONE state (notify HHS). Report on W-4 or equivalent, mail/magnetic/electronic. State deadlines shorter than 20 days per state unit. Local file for US-FED-017, which had none.

instrument_name: 29 U.S.C. 2102 WARN Act notice (U.S. Code 2024 ed.) + DOL Last Paycheck page
figure_or_rule_carried: Federal final pay: 'Employers are not required by federal law to give former employees their final paycheck immediately' (DOL) - final-pay timing and vacation payout are state law (per state unit); FLSA wages due by the regular payday. WARN: 60-day written notice before a plant closing or mass layoff (pay in lieu = back pay liability, 2104); payroll relevance limited to pay-in-lieu. No federal severance obligation. Final W-2 may be furnished early on request (US-FED-016).

instrument_name: 29 U.S.C. 2612 FMLA leave entitlement (U.S. Code 2024 ed.)
figure_or_rule_carried: Eligible employee: up to 12 workweeks in a 12-month period (26 for military caregiver), which may be UNPAID; employee may elect or employer may require substitution of accrued paid vacation/personal/family leave. No federal paid sick leave or paid annual leave for private employers (paid leave = state law / state PFML per state unit). Federal contractors: EO 13706 paid sick leave page exists (DOL WHD) - accrual figures not transcribed in this pass.

instrument_name: 29 CFR 5.5(a)(3) Davis-Bacon contract clauses - payrolls and basic records, weekly certified payroll (eCFR current)
figure_or_rule_carried: On DBA/Related-Acts covered contracts (federal construction over 2,000 - US-FED-019): contractor submits certified payrolls WEEKLY for each week covered work is performed, to the contracting agency (or applicant/sponsor/owner); prime contractor responsible for subcontractors' payrolls; records kept 3 years. Optional form WH-347. State prevailing-wage certified payroll per state unit.

instrument_name: IRS Publication 15 (2026) sec. 15 Special Rules for Various Types of Services and Payments (table) + sec. 3 family employees + state/local government employers
article_or_section: Sec. 3 (Child employed by parents); sec. 15 table pp. 47-52; State and local government employers
figure_or_rule_carried: Household (domestic) employees: FIT withholding only if both agree; FICA if cash wages 3,000+ in 2026 (exempt under age 18 unless principal occupation); FUTA if 1,000+ cash wages in any quarter of current or prior year. Child under 18 employed by parent's sole proprietorship/parents-only partnership: FICA exempt; FUTA exempt under 21; domestic work for parent: FICA exempt under 21. Spouse employed by spouse: FICA taxable if in course of spouse's business, FUTA exempt. Parent employed by child: FUTA exempt. Students at private school/college: FIT withheld, FICA and FUTA exempt; public school: FICA exempt unless sec. 218 agreement; work-experience full-time student: FICA taxable, FUTA exempt unless program established for an employer; student nurse nominal pay: FICA exempt. State/local government: FIT withheld, no FUTA, FICA with exceptions (sec. 218 / Medicare-only). Farmworkers: US-FEDR3-006 (Form 943). Ministers: US-FED-030. Statutory employees: US-FEDR3-005. Severance pay = wages for FIT, FICA and FUTA.

instrument_name: P.L. 119-21 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act, enacted 2025-07-04) - payroll-relevant changes as implemented in IRS 2026 employer publications
article_or_section: W-2/W-3 instructions 2026 What's New; Pub. 15 2026 What's New; Pub. 15-B 2026 What's New; Pub. 15-T 2026 What's New

(2) Trump accounts: from 2026-07-04 employer may contribute up to 2,500/yr excluded from income under a sec. 128 program (indexed after 2027; account limit 5,000) - W-2 Box 12 TA. (3) Dependent care exclusion 7,500. (4) Moving and bicycle-commuting exclusions eliminated. (5) Info-return/W-2 no-withholding threshold 2,000. (6) Rates 10-37% and 22%/37% supplemental made permanent. TY2025 reporting penalty relief only (Notice 2025-62).
